title: LuckRead D1-04 W07 RevenueCat Webhook Inbox PostgreSQL Schema Slice

dependencies.sourceBoundary: RevenueCat is a separate provider inbox and must not change payment_provider_events.provider='hyperswitch'.

revenuecat_webhook_events.terminalRule: Once state leaves RECEIVED the receipt is immutable.
revenuecat_webhook_events.payloadRule: Store bounded object event_data_json; do not store raw_body or subscriber_attributes columns.

revenuecat_webhook_event_conflicts.occurrenceRule: Every update increments occurrence_count by exactly one and never moves last_seen_at backwards.
revenuecat_webhook_event_conflicts.referenceRule: A conflict references the matching app_id/event_id and immutable first receipt payload_sha256.

postgresMappings.integer: Map event_timestamp_ms and occurrence_count to BIGINT; preserve the source safe-integer bound for event_timestamp_ms.
postgresMappings.time: Map ISO-8601 TEXT received_at, processed_at, first_seen_at and last_seen_at values to TIMESTAMPTZ and compare as instants.
postgresMappings.json: Keep event_data_json as TEXT with bounded length and PostgreSQL JSONB object-shape validation; never persist raw webhook bytes.
postgresMappings.deduplication: Preserve UNIQUE(app_id,event_id) for the first receipt and UNIQUE(app_id,event_id,incoming_payload_sha256) for each distinct conflicting payload.
postgresMappings.conflict: Conflict rows reference the immutable first receipt hash; occurrence_count advances exactly one per update and last_seen_at is monotonic.
postgresMappings.immutability: Receipt identity/payload is immutable; a receipt becomes fully immutable once state leaves RECEIVED. Event and conflict receipts are retained.
postgresMappings.providerIsolation: RevenueCat remains separate from the Hyperswitch payment_provider_events table and its provider CHECK constraint.
postgresMappings.privacy: Do not add raw_body, subscriber_attributes, PAN/CVC, API keys, browser client secrets or provider credentials.
postgresMappings.authority: W07 owns D1-04 webhook receipt and conflict facts. Applying RevenueCat events to D1-01 entitlement/subscription state is a separate runtime concern and is not implemented by this schema slice.

requiredPositiveCases: first RevenueCat receipt is inserted with bounded object payload and SHA-256 digest
one distinct payload conflict references the immutable first receipt
repeated conflicting payload advances occurrence_count by exactly one and last_seen_at monotonically
a RECEIVED event can be marked APPLIED with processed_at and outcome_code
cumulative PostgreSQL catalog contains twelve tables, twenty-five explicit indexes, fifty-six source triggers, four trigger functions and zero foreign keys
requiredNegativeCases: duplicate app_id and event_id cannot replace the first receipt
event payload identity, provider metadata and received_at cannot be rewritten
processed RevenueCat receipts cannot be updated or deleted
a conflict cannot reference a missing or mismatched first receipt
existing and incoming payload hashes must be valid lowercase SHA-256 and must differ
duplicate app_id, event_id and incoming_payload_sha256 conflicts are rejected
conflict identity cannot be rewritten and occurrence_count cannot skip or move backwards
RevenueCat inbox tables contain no raw_body or subscriber_attributes fields
conflict audit records cannot be deleted

nextGate: PAY-006 refunds and billing documents local PostgreSQL 18.6 rehearsal only. Payment-method revocation remains a separate slice; remote runner and Neon cutover remain unauthorized.
